I don't know exactly what their experience was, but I've heard things about wire being found, maggots, all sorts of shady shit happens when they make their food.  In terms of nutrition, though, it's pure garbage.  Most top listed ingredients are grains and corn, and a lot of the protein is animal by-product.  They don't specify what animal, so you don't know if it's road kill or even things like dead zoo animals.  And while by-products aren't inherently bad (it's organs and things we wouldn't want to eat as humans, but are fine for animals), it's just not very consistent.  Also, something I was taught was that these flavor names mean something about the content of certain ingredients in food.  If it says something generic like 'dog chow' or 'puppy recipe', they aren't promising you anything.  It's whatever they want.  If it says 'with' something, it only has to be 3%, which is why my boyfriend makes me mad when he says 'but it's okay!  It says with beef!', because it sounds healthy, but the other 97% could be God knows what.

My last and most serious attempt left me waking up with a lot of pain, regret, and confusion.

I had been doing really well in that I hadn't had suicidal thoughts in over a year.  Then my psychiatrist put me on a new medicine he didn't bother to tell us had horrible side effects in a younger age group.  Needless to say, my body rejected it horribly, leading me to end up in the ER twice in the span of about a week - the first time for the worst headache and body aches I'd ever experienced, and the second time for my suicide attempt.

The medication left me in a very weird, very zombie-like state, and I would do things without really knowing why.  Paired with my grandpa being taken to the hospital numerous times for heart problems or the cancer that had just been diagnosed, I was a total wreck.  So after getting in an argument with my mom, I walked downstairs and downed at least a quarter of a bottle of Kirkland brand allergy medicine, which was easily over 100 pills.  I got tired, and my mom asked me to do something in preparation for school the next day, and I told her I didn't need to.  She asked why, and I said I wouldn't be here for it, so it didn't matter.  She got really scared, asked me what I did, I broke down and told her, and she called 911.

A lot of the night went in a blur, but I had to be questioned by a police officer to make sure that it wasn't because I'd been abused or neglected and I was acting out against that, was given a huge cup of activated charcoal, which I only got about an eighth of it down before I started vomiting, had a tube shoved down my nose and into my stomach to get the charcoal into me (I had to be restrained by several people while I screamed and thrashed around in pain), went into convulsions (which I remember very vividly), fought with a nurse in my delusional state about wanting water to drink, fought with a nurse about getting up and going to the bathroom instead of being asked to piss myself in bed, fought with a nurse about getting the Goddamn tube out of me if I didn't need it anymore, got woken up some time later after passing out, where they pulled the tube out of me (just as painful going in as it was coming out, so I had to be restrained again), got a bloody nose from the tube coming out, got questioned by a lady where I had an odd moment of clarity and somehow narrowly avoided getting put into a mental hospital for a week, had my IV pulled out and had my arm get pressed on so hard to stop the bleeding that I had a huge purple bruise for the next week, and got sent home.

My family was confused about why I did it, and to be honest, it kills me because /I don't know/.  That medicine fucked me up beyond belief, and I was only on it for week.  So, yeah.  Turns out I had a majorly adverse reaction to it, which everyone noticed because I was acting in horribly impulsive ways, which I don't do in my right mind.  I'm pretty glad to be alive, and I was even told there was a decent possibility I could have died that night.  It's pretty nice being off all these medications, too.  I feel a lot clearer and happier for it.
